title: Magic-item readiness silently skips a clause with an unrecognized scope kind
description:
Verified at main f4b3461. packages/core/src/state/itemExecutionReadiness.ts:19-31 inSelectedScope returns false for any clause scope whose kind is neither 'parent' nor a matching 'variant', and :76-77 then skips that clause entirely, so a clause with a malformed or unrecognized scope CANNOT block the operation. assertMagicItemOperationReady is the only live runtime capability gate (called from state/itemState.ts:1888) and is otherwise correctly fail-closed.

No such clause exists in the committed pack, so this is latent. ADR 0020 section 3 makes it a defect regardless: 'any gate, report, or predicate that reads an unbound or unrecognized item as satisfied is a defect, not a green.' Recorded as ar72 D-9b in docs/audits/rules-awareness-transition/2026-07-29-current-state-claim-and-defect-map.md.

Blocker B5 of 2026-07-30-integrated-transition-design.md: the contract cannot serve as pilot capability evidence (probe P8, magic-item:ammunition-1-2-or-3 / hit-target) until an unrecognized scope fails closed.
acceptance_criteria: An unrecognized clause scope kind fails closed rather than being skipped; a test feeds a malformed scope and asserts ItemExecutionReadinessError; existing parent/variant scope behavior is unchanged and its tests still pass.
